objective: Make all text file I/O in the scoped workflow scripts and hooks explicitly use UTF-8 and prove non-ASCII content round-trips without corruption.
requirements: Add encoding="utf-8" to every text-mode Path.read_text, Path.write_text, Path.open, and os.fdopen operation in the four scoped files.
Preserve all existing workflow behavior and pure-ASCII artifact bytes while changing only the selected text encoding.
Add focused regression coverage for the scoped source calls, orchestrator helper round-tripping of an em dash, curly quote, and non-Latin character, and literal em-dash output from ADR creation.
Leave .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py and .ai/hooks/post_tool_use.py unchanged because their text I/O already specifies UTF-8.

files_to_modify.purpose: Specify UTF-8 for every text read, write, append, and file-descriptor stream used by the orchestrator.
Specify UTF-8 for all review artifact and state text I/O.
Specify UTF-8 when reading context and constitution text.
Specify UTF-8 when reading event and implementation-note text.

files_to_create.purpose: Provide focused static and behavioral regression tests for explicit UTF-8 text I/O, Unicode helper round-tripping, and ADR template output.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every text-mode read_text, write_text, Path.open, and os.fdopen call in the four scoped files explicitly specifies encoding="utf-8".
The orchestrator's artifact helpers round-trip text containing an em dash, curly quote, and non-Latin character identically.
ADR creation writes a Supersedes line containing a literal em dash and no Unicode replacement character.
The complete repository test suite passes after the encoding-only change.

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
Do not change behavior other than selecting UTF-8 for text I/O.
Do not refactor, rename, reformat, or restructure unrelated code.
Do not change json.dumps ensure_ascii behavior.
Do not weaken or delete existing tests.
Restrict implementation changes to the four named workflow files and the declared focused test file.
risks: A naive textual count can misclassify low-level os.open calls, so the source audit should distinguish text stream APIs from descriptor creation.
Multiline calls and context-manager opens can be missed by grep-style checks; an AST-based regression test is safer.
Tests that rely on the host locale may pass on UTF-8 systems despite a regression, so tests must inspect explicit call arguments as well as exercising Unicode behavior.
The working tree already contains unrelated changes; implementation must avoid touching or overwriting them.
test_strategy: Add an AST-based audit covering all four scoped files and requiring UTF-8 on each text stream operation while excluding low-level descriptor-only os.open.
Exercise append_context_block and read_context in an isolated task directory with representative punctuation and non-Latin text.
Exercise run_adr in an isolated directory and assert the generated UTF-8 text contains the exact Supersedes em dash and no replacement character.
Run the focused UTF-8 test module, then run the full unittest discovery suite; CI provides the required Python 3.9 and 3.12 matrix coverage.
